meaning:
στρωννύω or στρώννυμι
(seeBl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), [in LXX for יַצַע hoph., etc. ;]
to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Mat.21:8, Mrk.11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Act.9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Eze.23:41), Mrk.14:15, Luk.22:12.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: A very great multitude spread their clothes on the road. Others cut branches from the trees, and spread them on the road.
Many spread their garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees, and spreading them on the road.
He will show you a large, furnished upper room. Make preparations there.”
